title: Why is an immutable value class inherently thread-safe?
shortTitle: Why is an immutable value class inherently thread-safe?
keyPoints: Thread safety problems come from shared mutable state – immutable objects have no mutable state
Once constructed, all fields are final and never change – no race conditions possible
The JMM guarantees that final fields are safely published after the constructor completes
No synchronization, no volatile, no locks needed – zero concurrency overhead
Examples: String, BigDecimal, LocalDate, Integer – all immutable and freely shared across threads

s1_definition.oneliner: An immutable object has no mutable state, so there is nothing for threads to race on. The Java Memory Model guarantees final fields are visible to all threads after construction. No synchronization needed.
s1_definition.profdef:
Why immutable = thread-safe:

- **No shared mutable state.** Thread safety bugs require mutability. If fields never change, there is no race condition.
- **Final field guarantee.** The JMM ensures that final fields are safely published to all threads after the constructor completes.
- **Zero overhead.** No synchronized blocks, no volatile fields, no AtomicReference needed.
s1_definition.analogy: A printed bank statement can be shared with any number of auditors simultaneously. None of them can modify it, so there is no conflict. A mutable spreadsheet, on the other hand, needs locking to prevent two auditors from editing the same cell at the same time.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Mutable state + multiple threads = race conditions, lost updates, dirty reads
    → needs synchronized, volatile, locks

  Immutable state + any threads = safe, no conflicts, no locks
    → final fields guaranteed visible after construction (JMM)
    → zero synchronization overhead

  Pattern: AtomicReference<ImmutableState>
    read → compute new immutable state → CAS-swap → no locks
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
An immutable object is inherently thread-safe because there is no mutable state for threads to conflict on. Once constructed, all final fields are visible to every thread (guaranteed by the Java Memory Model), and no thread can modify them. No synchronization, no volatile, no locks needed.

This is why String, BigDecimal, and LocalDate can be freely shared across any number of threads. In banking, immutable snapshots of account state are safe for concurrent processing without any locking overhead.

One sentence to remember: immutable means no shared mutable state, no race conditions, no locks – thread-safe by construction.
